intro: If you're planning a trip out to Ban Rai, the rice fields, or the Huai Kha Khaeng forest and want a stay that isn't bunched up in Uthai Thani town — Numhom Resort is a name drivers passing through the Thap Than area keep mentioning. It's a 3-star garden bungalow resort in Thap Than sub-district, Thap Than District, sitting roughly midway between town and Ban Rai. Every room is air-conditioned with a balcony, several bungalows are set in front of a small pond, and there's a green garden, a children's playground, an on-site restaurant and free parking at your door. It's a quiet, rural feel, with rooms from around ฿650/night.

body.html: What makes Numhom Resort interesting is its position as a midway stop between Uthai Thani town and Ban Rai District. Travellers heading out to the western side of the province — the rice fields, viewpoints, or Huai Kha Khaeng forest — often don't want to stay deep in town and double back every day. This sits in the Thap Than area, right on the way, so getting out there is easier. And because it's a garden bungalow resort rather than a block of square rooms, you get a quieter feel and more greenery than an in-town stay.

Rooms are bungalows and air-con rooms, all with a balcony. There's a good spread to choose from: a Superior with twin beds, a Standard with a king and balcony, a one-bedroom bungalow, and a four-bed family room for bigger groups. Real reviews praise clean, spacious, private rooms with comfy beds, and several bungalows sit right in front of a small pond — open the door to garden and water. It's a well-kept stay in the few-hundred-to-low-thousands-of-baht range.

What families like is the on-site playground and the big garden where kids can run around. Parents travelling with children often say they feel relaxed here, because the resort is quiet, with little traffic and a space for kids to play without going anywhere. There's also an on-site restaurant, a BBQ area and a small convenience store, so you don't have to drive far for food in the evening — a real help, since the surroundings are rural with few shops.
"Clean, spacious and private rooms, the bungalow sits in front of a little pond, lovely quiet atmosphere, warm and welcoming staff, and the kids loved the playground — great value."

The praise that comes up most in reviews is the peace and quiet, the cleanliness, and the welcome from the staff. Many say they arrive and genuinely unwind — nothing hectic, just a coffee looking out at the garden. There's 24-hour reception, a laundry service, and free parking at your door, which is handy for self-drivers. Overall it feels more like staying at a country garden home than at a hotel.

To be straight with you, the main limitation is the rural location away from Uthai Thani town. If you want to step out and find the town market, the Sakae Krang riverside or a coffee shop straight away, this isn't it — it's about a 20-minute drive into town. The surroundings are quiet and dark at night with few shops, so it's better suited to those with a car than to anyone without transport. And because the resort also hosts functions and has karaoke, there can be some noise when an event is on — worth checking with the property if you want complete quiet.

Overall, Numhom Resort scores around 9.1 out of 10 on Agoda from over 160 real reviews, with guests praising the cleanliness, the peace and quiet, the garden bungalows and the staff welcome. It isn't a luxury resort, but measured on its country-garden feel, clean rooms, playground, on-site restaurant, free parking, and rates from around ฿650 (rising with season and room type) — it's a well-judged base for families and drivers heading out to the Ban Rai side.

A tip drawn from the reviews: pick a bungalow set in front of the pond for the full feel, and if you're a bigger group, look at the four-bed family room. Driving yourself is easiest, since you'll use the car both into town and out west. Book ahead over long weekends as there aren't many rooms — and if you want complete quiet, ask the property whether there's a function or karaoke on the dates you're staying.

faq.q: Where is Numhom Resort in Uthai Thani, and what's nearby?
faq.a: Numhom Resort is at 4/2 Moo 6, Thap Than, Thap Than District, Uthai Thani. Thap Than market is about a 5-minute drive, Uthai Thani town and the market roughly 20 minutes, and the Sakae Krang River about 22 minutes. It's a handy midway stop on the way out to Ban Rai District and the Huai Kha Khaeng forest.

faq.q: How much does Numhom Resort cost, and what room types are there?
faq.a: Rates start from around ฿650/night for a Superior twin. There are Superior, Standard (king with balcony), a one-bedroom bungalow, and a four-bed family room. All rooms are air-conditioned with a balcony and en-suite bathroom. Prices rise with season and room type, so compare a few platforms before booking.

faq.q: Is Numhom Resort good for kids — is there a playground?
faq.a: Yes — there's an on-site playground and a big garden where kids can run around. The resort is quiet with little traffic, so parents with children often say they feel relaxed. There's also an on-site restaurant and a small convenience store, so you don't have to drive far for food in the evening.

faq.q: Is Numhom Resort a good base for visiting Ban Rai?
faq.a: Very much so — the Thap Than location sits roughly midway between Uthai Thani town and Ban Rai District, right on the way. Travellers heading out to the rice fields, viewpoints or the Huai Kha Khaeng forest on the western side of the province often don't want to stay deep in town and double back daily, so heading out from here is easier.

faq.q: Is Numhom Resort quiet — anything to watch out for?
faq.a: Overall it's peaceful, with a country-garden feel, and real reviews praise the restful atmosphere and cleanliness. That said, the resort also hosts functions and has karaoke, so there can be some noise when an event is on. If you want complete quiet, ask the property whether there's an event on your dates and pick a bungalow away from the function area.

faq.q: Who is Numhom Resort best for?
faq.a: It's a strong fit for families with kids and drivers heading out to the Ban Rai side who want quiet garden bungalows, a playground and an on-site restaurant on a comfortable budget. It's less ideal for travellers without a car who want a central, walkable stay, as it's in the Thap Than area and needs a drive into town.
